- **Approximate records:** ~2,000-6,500 institutions (depending on filters — degree-granting Title IV institutions)
- **Geographic scope:** National (all U.S.)

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
The institution count range is wide because it depends on analytical choices we'll refine during planning — for example, whether to include community colleges (which have structurally different graduation rates due to transfer students) or focus on 4-year institutions only. IPEDS graduation rates track first-time, full-time (FTFT) students, which systematically undercounts outcomes for institutions serving more part-time and transfer students. This is itself part of the "chicken-or-egg" story you're investigating.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

All relevant data lives at the institution level, identified by `unitid` (6-digit IPEDS institution ID). No school-level or district-level data is needed.

**Rationale:** The research question explicitly concerns colleges/universities. All key variables (graduation rates, admission rates, Pell Grant shares, URM enrollment, student-faculty ratios, instructional expenditures, retention rates, institutional sector) are available at the institution level through IPEDS, Scorecard, and FSA datasets. The join key `unitid` links all three sources.

---

## 2. Candidate Endpoints

| # | Endpoint | Source | Dataset Path | Description | Years Available | Type |
|---|----------|--------|-------------|-------------|-----------------|------|
| 1 | IPEDS Directory | IPEDS | `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_directory` | Institution characteristics: sector, control, HBCU, level, locale, open admissions, total enrollment | 1980-2023 | Single |
| 2 | IPEDS Admissions-Enrollment | IPEDS | `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_admissions-enrollment` | Applicants, admitted, enrolled, admission rate, yield rate, SAT/ACT scores | 2001-2023 | Single |
| 3 | IPEDS Graduation Rates | IPEDS | `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_grad-rates` | 4-year, 5-year, 6-year graduation rates; cohort sizes; transfer-out rates; by race/sex | 1996-2022 | Single |
| 4 | IPEDS Fall Enrollment by Race | IPEDS | `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_fall-enrollment-race_{year}` | Enrollment disaggregated by race, sex, level, FT/PT, class level, degree-seeking | 1986-2022 | Yearly |
| 5 | IPEDS Student-Faculty Ratio | IPEDS | `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_student-faculty-ratio` | Student-to-faculty ratio, instructional FTE faculty | 2009-2020 | Single |
| 6 | IPEDS Finance | IPEDS | `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_finance` | Revenue, expenditures (instruction, student services, etc.), endowment, assets | 1987-2022 | Single |
| 7 | IPEDS Fall Retention | IPEDS | `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_fall-retention` | FT and PT first-time student retention rates | 2003-2020 | Single |
| 8 | FSA Grants | FSA | `fsa/colleges_fsa_grants` | Pell Grant recipients and disbursements by institution | 1999-2021 | Single |
| 9 | Scorecard Student Characteristics | Scorecard | `scorecard/colleges_scorecard_student_body_nslds` | Pct Pell, pct first-gen, pct by race, median family income (Title IV recipients only) | 1997-2016 | Single |
| 10 | IPEDS SFA Grants and Net Price | IPEDS | `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_sfa_grants_and_net_price` | Net price by income level, grant amounts, number of students | 2008-2021 | Single |
| 11 | IPEDS Outcome Measures | IPEDS | `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_outcome-measures` | Broader completion rates including part-time and transfer students (8-year window) | 2015-2022 | Single |

**Primary analysis endpoints:** #1-8 form the core dataset. #9-11 are supplementary/enrichment.

---

## 3. Key Variables

### Core Outcome Variable

| Variable | Endpoint | Portal Column Name | Type | Description | Notes |
|----------|----------|--------------------|------|-------------|-------|
| Graduation rate (150% time) | IPEDS Grad Rates | `completion_rate_150pct` | Float | 6-yr rate for 4-yr institutions | **CRITICAL:** Tracks ONLY first-time, full-time, fall-entering students. Filter to `race==99, sex==99` for totals. |
| Graduation rate (100% time) | IPEDS Grad Rates | `completers_100pct` | Int | On-time completers count | Must divide by `cohort_adj_150pct` |
| Transfer-out rate | IPEDS Grad Rates | `transfers_out` | Int | Students who transferred out | Needed to contextualize non-completion |
| Cohort size | IPEDS Grad Rates | `cohort_adj_150pct` | Int | Adjusted cohort count | Denominator for rate calculations |

### Core Predictor: Selectivity

| Variable | Endpoint | Portal Column Name | Type | Description | Notes |
|----------|----------|--------------------|------|-------------|-------|
| Admission rate | IPEDS Admissions | `admit_rate` | Float | Admitted / Applied | May need to compute manually from `number_admitted / number_applied`. **Filter `sex==99` for totals** (data disaggregated by sex). |
| Total applicants | IPEDS Admissions | `number_applied` | Int | Total applications received | Portal name differs from docs (`applicants_total` documented, `number_applied` actual) |
| Total admitted | IPEDS Admissions | `number_admitted` | Int | Total students admitted | Portal name differs from docs (`admissions_total` documented, `number_admitted` actual) |
| SAT Math 25th pctile | IPEDS Admissions | `sat_math_25` | Int | SAT Math 25th percentile | Alternative selectivity measure |
| SAT Math 75th pctile | IPEDS Admissions | `sat_math_75` | Int | SAT Math 75th percentile | |
| ACT Composite 25th pctile | IPEDS Admissions | `act_composite_25` | Int | ACT Composite 25th percentile | |
| ACT Composite 75th pctile | IPEDS Admissions | `act_composite_75` | Int | ACT Composite 75th percentile | |
| Open admissions | IPEDS Directory | `open_admissions` | Int (0/1) | Open admissions policy indicator | Identifies non-selective institutions |

### Financial Aid Dependency / Economic Context

| Variable | Endpoint | Portal Column Name | Type | Description | Notes |
|----------|----------|--------------------|------|-------------|-------|
| Pell Grant recipients (count) | FSA Grants | `grant_recipients_unitid` | Int | Number of Pell recipients at institution | Filter `grant_type==1` (Pell) |
| Pell disbursements | FSA Grants | `value_grants_disbursed_unitid` | Float | Total Pell $ disbursed | Filter `grant_type==1` |
| Pell avg amount | FSA Grants | `pell_avg_amount` | Float | Average Pell amount | |
| Pct receiving Pell (Scorecard) | Scorecard Student Chars | `pct_pell` | Float | Share of students on Pell | **Title IV recipients only** -- selection bias at wealthy institutions |
| Pct first-generation | Scorecard Student Chars | `pct_first_gen` | Float | Share first-generation students | |
| Median family income | Scorecard Student Chars | `median_family_income` | Float | Median family income of students | |
| Pct receiving any aid (IPEDS) | IPEDS SFA All Undergrads | `percent_of_students` | Float | Share receiving any aid | Filter by `type_of_aid` code |
| Net price by income | IPEDS SFA Grants/Net Price | `net_price` | Int | Net price after grants by income bracket | Filter by `income_level` (1-5) |

### Underserved / Historically Disadvantaged Populations

| Variable | Endpoint | Portal Column Name | Type | Description | Notes |
|----------|----------|--------------------|------|-------------|-------|
| Enrollment by race | IPEDS Fall Enrollment (Race) | `enrollment_fall` | Int | Fall enrollment count by race | Filter by `race` codes: 2=Black, 3=Hispanic, 5=AIAN, 6=NHPI. Must compute URM shares manually. |
| Pct Black (Scorecard) | Scorecard Student Chars | `pct_black` | Float | Share Black students | Title IV recipients only |
| Pct Hispanic (Scorecard) | Scorecard Student Chars | `pct_hispanic` | Float | Share Hispanic students | Title IV recipients only |
| Pct Asian (Scorecard) | Scorecard Student Chars | `pct_asian` | Float | Share Asian students | |
| Pct White (Scorecard) | Scorecard Student Chars | `pct_white` | Float | Share White students | |
| HBCU indicator | IPEDS Directory | `hbcu` | Int (0/1) | HBCU status | |
| Tribal college indicator | IPEDS Directory | `tribal_college` | Int (0/1) | Tribal college status | |

### Institutional Resources

| Variable | Endpoint | Portal Column Name | Type | Description | Notes |
|----------|----------|--------------------|------|-------------|-------|
| Student-faculty ratio | IPEDS Student-Faculty Ratio | `student_faculty_ratio` | Float | Student-to-faculty ratio | Available 2009-2020 |
| Instructional FTE faculty | IPEDS Student-Faculty Ratio | `instructional_fte` | Int | FTE instructional staff | |
| Instruction expenditure | IPEDS Finance | `exp_instruction` | Float | Instruction spending (total) | **CRITICAL:** GASB vs FASB -- cannot compare public and private directly |
| Total expenditure | IPEDS Finance | `exp_total` | Float | Total expenditure | |
| Student services expense | IPEDS Finance | `exp_student_services` | Float | Student services spending | |
| Endowment | IPEDS Finance | `endowment_eoy` | Float | End-of-year endowment | |
| FTE enrollment | IPEDS Enrollment FTE | `fte_total` (or `est_fte`) | Int | Total FTE for per-student calculations | Needed to compute expenditure per FTE |

### Institutional Characteristics (Sector / Control)

| Variable | Endpoint | Portal Column Name | Type | Description | Notes |
|----------|----------|--------------------|------|-------------|-------|
| Institutional control | IPEDS Directory | `inst_control` | Int | 1=Public, 2=Private nonprofit, 3=Private for-profit | |
| Institution level | IPEDS Directory | `institution_level` | Int | 1=<2yr, 2=2yr, **4**=4yr+ | **No code 3** |
| Sector | IPEDS Directory | `sector` | Int | Combined control x level (1-9) | |
| Degree-granting | IPEDS Directory | `degree_granting` | Int (0/1) | Degree-granting status | Filter to `==1` |
| Locale | IPEDS Directory | `locale` | Int | Urban-centric locale code | |
| Total enrollment | IPEDS Directory | `enrollment_total` | Int | Total enrollment | For size context |

### Retention (Leading Indicator)

| Variable | Endpoint | Portal Column Name | Type | Description | Notes |
|----------|----------|--------------------|------|-------------|-------|
| FT retention rate | IPEDS Fall Retention | Verify via codebook (NCES: `ret_pcf`) | Float | Full-time first-time retention rate | First-time students only; same cohort limitation as grad rates |
| PT retention rate | IPEDS Fall Retention | Verify via codebook (NCES: `ret_pcp`) | Float | Part-time first-time retention rate | |

---

## 4. Variables Flagged for Deep-Dive

| # | Variable / Topic | Reason for Deep-Dive |
|---|-----------------|---------------------|
| 1 | `completion_rate_150pct` (graduation rate) | **CRITICAL:** Tracks only first-time, full-time, fall-entering students -- excludes ~40% transfers, ~40% part-time. At community colleges, may represent <25% of students. This limitation is THE central methodological caveat for the entire analysis. Need source-researcher to document exact cohort definition, subcohort filtering, and Outcome Measures alternative. |
| 2 | `admit_rate` vs computed rate | Portal may provide `admit_rate` directly OR may require computing from `number_admitted / number_applied`. Need to verify actual column availability and whether `admit_rate` is pre-computed or needs calculation. Also: **must filter `sex==99`** to get institution-level totals (data is disaggregated by sex). |
| 3 | URM enrollment share computation | IPEDS Fall Enrollment (Race) provides counts by race code, not pre-computed URM shares. Need to: (a) verify race code values in actual data, (b) define URM operationally (Black + Hispanic + AIAN + NHPI? or different?), (c) handle pre-2010 race category changes (Asian included Pacific Islanders; Two-or-more not collected). |
| 4 | Pell share: FSA vs Scorecard vs IPEDS SFA | Three sources provide Pell data with different populations: FSA grants (all Pell recipients at institution), Scorecard `pct_pell` (Title IV recipients only -- overrepresents low-income), IPEDS SFA (various aid populations). Need to determine which is most appropriate denominator for "share of students on Pell." |
| 5 | Finance data: GASB vs FASB | IPEDS finance uses GASB for public institutions and FASB for private institutions -- different accounting standards make direct cross-sector comparison of expenditures problematic. Need source-researcher to identify which variables are comparable and which are not, and whether instructional expenditure per FTE is valid cross-sector. |
| 6 | Finance data year availability | IPEDS skill warns finance data may only be available through **2017** in Portal mirrors (despite nominal 1987-2022 range). This is a significant data lag that could limit analysis to older years. Needs verification during Stage 5 fetch. |
| 7 | Retention rate variable names | Portal variable names for fall-retention dataset are not fully verified in skill documentation (listed as NCES names `ret_pcf`, `ret_pcp`). Need to fetch sample data to confirm actual Portal column names. |
| 8 | Scorecard student characteristics year coverage | Portal data covers 1997-2016 only, not the 2020-2023 range of interest. If analysis targets recent years, Scorecard demographic percentages will need to come from IPEDS Fall Enrollment (Race) instead, requiring manual computation. |
| 9 | `subcohort` filtering in grad rates | IPEDS graduation rates dataset contains multiple subcohort rows per institution (overall, Pell, subsidized loan, neither). Need to identify correct `subcohort` code for overall graduation rate vs. Pell-specific rate. |
| 10 | Instructional expenditure per FTE | Requires joining IPEDS Finance (`exp_instruction`) with IPEDS Enrollment FTE (`fte_total` or `est_fte`). FTE calculation methods vary (credit-hour vs clock-hour institutions). Need to verify join compatibility and FTE definition. |

---

## 5. Limitations Encountered

| # | Limitation | Impact | Recommended Resolution |
|---|-----------|--------|------------------------|
| 1 | IPEDS graduation rates track only FTFT students | The outcome variable itself embeds selectivity bias -- institutions with more traditional students (full-time, first-time) have more representative graduation rates. This is actually the CORE of the research question. | Document limitation prominently in analysis. Consider supplementing with IPEDS Outcome Measures (2015-2022) which track part-time and transfer students. |
| 2 | IPEDS Finance data may end at 2017 in Portal mirrors | Limits expenditure-per-FTE analysis to potentially older years, creating a year mismatch with other variables (admissions, grad rates available to 2022) | Verify actual availability during fetch. If confirmed, either limit all variables to 2017 or analyze finance variables on a different (overlapping) year. |
| 3 | Scorecard student characteristics end at 2016 | Cannot get pre-computed `pct_pell`, `pct_first_gen`, `pct_black` etc. for recent years from Scorecard | Compute URM shares from IPEDS Fall Enrollment (Race) data. Compute Pell share from FSA grants data + IPEDS enrollment denominator. |
| 4 | GASB/FASB accounting differences | Cannot directly compare expenditure levels between public and private institutions | Either analyze within sector only, or use expenditure *ranks* rather than levels for cross-sector analysis. Data scientist skill's statistical-modeling reference may have guidance. |
| 5 | Admissions data variable name discrepancy | Portal uses `number_applied`/`number_admitted` not `applicants_total`/`admissions_total` as documented in some references | Use verified Portal names from IPEDS source skill. Validate with sample fetch in Stage 5. |
| 6 | Open-admissions institutions lack admission rate | Institutions with `open_admissions==1` will have missing/meaningless admission rates | Must decide: exclude open-admissions institutions from selectivity analysis, or code them as a separate category (e.g., admit_rate = 100%). |
| 7 | Student-faculty ratio available only 2009-2020 | Narrower year range than other variables | Use latest available overlapping year (likely 2020). |
| 8 | Race category changes pre-2010 | Pre-2010: Asian included Pacific Islanders; "Two or more races" not collected | Limit race analysis to post-2010 data, or document the break in series. |

---

## 6. Completeness Assessment

- [x] Schools level searched: N/A (not relevant -- postsecondary question)
- [x] Districts level searched: N/A (not relevant -- postsecondary question)
- [x] Colleges level searched: **Yes** -- comprehensive search of all IPEDS, Scorecard, and FSA endpoints
- [x] Multiple sources considered:
  - **IPEDS**: Directory, Admissions, Graduation Rates, Fall Enrollment (Race), Student-Faculty Ratio, Finance, Fall Retention, Enrollment FTE, SFA Grants/Net Price, Outcome Measures -- all checked
  - **College Scorecard**: Student Characteristics, Earnings, Institutional Characteristics -- checked
  - **FSA**: Grants, Loans -- checked
  - **NACUBO**: Endowments -- considered but IPEDS Finance `endowment_eoy` is more comprehensive
  - **PSEO**: Post-graduation employment -- noted as supplementary but not core to this question

---

## 7. Confidence Assessment

| Finding | Confidence | Rationale |
|---------|------------|-----------|
| Core endpoints identified (Directory, Admissions, Grad Rates, Enrollment by Race, S-F Ratio, Finance, Retention, FSA Grants) | **HIGH** | All endpoints verified in colleges-endpoints.md, datasets-reference.md, and source-specific skills. Dataset paths confirmed. |
| Variable names for Admissions and Grad Rates | **MEDIUM** | IPEDS source skill documents known discrepancies (e.g., `number_applied` vs `applicants_total`, `completion_rate_150pct` vs `grad_rate_150pct`). Verified Portal names from IPEDS SKILL.md but should confirm with actual data fetch. |
| Year coverage overlaps sufficient for analysis | **HIGH** | All core endpoints have data through at least 2020. Admissions to 2023, Grad Rates to 2022, Enrollment to 2022. Target year of ~2020-2022 is achievable for most variables. |
| Finance data availability through 2017+ | **LOW** | IPEDS skill explicitly warns Portal mirror may only have finance data through 2017. This is a significant constraint. Must verify during Stage 5 fetch. |
| Pell share computation approach | **MEDIUM** | Three possible sources with different populations. Recommendation: use FSA `grant_recipients_unitid` (Pell type) divided by IPEDS total enrollment for the broadest, most defensible measure. But this needs validation -- FSA counts may include graduate Pell recipients while enrollment may need to be filtered to undergrad. |
| Retention variable names | **LOW** | Portal column names not verified -- only NCES names (`ret_pcf`, `ret_pcp`) appear in documentation. Need actual data inspection. |
| IPEDS Admissions sex-filtering requirement | **HIGH** | Confirmed in IPEDS source skill: admissions data is disaggregated by sex, and unfiltered data contains duplicates. Must filter `sex==99` for institution totals. |

**Overall Confidence:** **MEDIUM-HIGH**

The core data landscape is well-mapped with high confidence. The two LOW-confidence items (finance year availability and retention variable names) are verification tasks that can be resolved early in Stage 5 fetch with sample data downloads. They do not block planning.

**LOW Confidence Items Requiring Resolution:**
1. **Finance data year cutoff**: Verify during first Stage 5 fetch whether `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_finance` contains data beyond 2017 in Portal mirrors
2. **Retention variable names**: Fetch a sample of `ipeds/colleges_ipeds_fall-retention` during Stage 5 to confirm actual column names

---

## Gaps and Limitations

- **Not searched:** NCES IPEDS Data Center directly (only searched Portal mirror data). Some variables (e.g., distance education enrollment) are available at NCES but not in Portal mirrors.
- **Not explored:** State-level policy variables (e.g., state appropriations per student, state need-based aid programs) that could be confounders. These would require external data sources beyond the Education Data Portal.
- **Not verified:** Actual data file column names -- all variable names are from documentation and source skills. Actual column names must be verified with sample fetches in Stage 5.
- **Scorecard population bias:** Scorecard student-characteristics data covers only Title IV aid recipients. At selective private institutions, this may represent only 30-50% of students, systematically overrepresenting lower-income students.

## Learning Signal

**Learning Signal:** Data -- College-university graduation rate analysis requires careful attention to three population-definition traps: (1) IPEDS grad rates track only FTFT students, (2) IPEDS admissions data is disaggregated by sex and must be filtered to `sex==99` for totals, (3) Scorecard demographics cover only Title IV recipients. All three introduce composition bias that must be documented.

## Recommendations

- **Proceed?** YES
- **Recommended target year:** 2020 or 2021 -- best overlap across all endpoints (admissions, grad rates, enrollment, S-F ratio, retention, FSA grants all available)
- **Primary join key:** `unitid` across all datasets
- **Population filter:** Start with `degree_granting==1` and `institution_level==4` (4-year institutions) for the core analysis, then consider extending to 2-year institutions as a robustness check
- **Deep-dive priority:** Items #1 (grad rate cohort definition), #4 (Pell share source selection), and #5 (GASB/FASB cross-sector comparability) should be resolved before plan creation
- **Supplementary analysis worth considering:** IPEDS Outcome Measures (2015-2022) provides completion rates for part-time and transfer students, which could serve as a robustness check against the FTFT limitation of standard graduation rates

## VARIABLES

### Critical Variables for This Analysis

| Variable | Type | Description | Coded Values | Notes |
|----------|------|-------------|--------------|-------|
| `unitid` | Int64 | IPEDS institution identifier (6-digit) | N/A — identifier | Primary join key to IPEDS/Scorecard |

| `grant_recipients_unitid` | Float64 | Number of grant recipients at institution | Positive count; sentinel codes -1,-2,-3 | Key numerator variable |
| `value_grants_disbursed_unitid` | Float64 | Total grant dollars disbursed | Positive dollars; sentinel codes -1,-2,-3 | |
| `allocation_flag` | Int64 | Whether data was allocated across multiple unitids | 0=No, 1=Yes, null=Not reported | Institutions with flag=1 may have split counts |
| `combined_flag` | Int64 | Whether data was combined from multiple OPEIDs | 0=No, 1=Yes, null=Not reported | |

### Coded Value Reference: grant_type

| Code | Meaning | Standard Action |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `1` | Federal Pell Grant | **Include** — this is the target variable |
| `2` | Federal Supplemental Educational Opportunity Grant (FSEOG) | Exclude from Pell analysis |
| `3` | TEACH Grant | Exclude from Pell analysis |
| `4` | Iraq and Afghanistan Service Grant | Exclude from Pell analysis |
| `5` | Children of Fallen Heroes Grant | Exclude from Pell analysis |

### Coded Value Reference: Missing Data Codes (Numeric Variables)

| Code | Meaning | Recommended Action |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| `-1` | Missing / not reported | Exclude from calculations; flag institution as having missing data |
| `-2` | Not applicable | Exclude from calculations; institution may not participate in this grant type |
| `-3` | Suppressed for privacy (small cell size) | Exclude from calculations; cannot recover the value; document suppression |
| `null` | No data available | Exclude from calculations; record or field not present |

### Variable-Specific Warnings

| Variable | Warning | Impact | Mitigation |
|----------|---------|--------|------------|
| `grant_recipients_unitid` | Float64 type despite being a count | May contain sentinel values -1,-2,-3 that look like small negative numbers | Filter `> 0` or explicitly exclude -1,-2,-3 before any aggregation |
| `grant_recipients_unitid` | Year-Round Pell (post-2017) may inflate recipient count | Recipient counts may slightly exceed unduplicated Pell headcount | For Pell share computation, this is likely a minor issue since both numerator and context are for the same year; document as caveat |
| `value_grants_disbursed_unitid` | Nominal dollars, not inflation-adjusted | Dollar comparisons across years are misleading without adjustment | Apply CPI adjustments if comparing dollar amounts across years; for Pell share (count-based), this is not relevant |
| `allocation_flag` | When `1`, the institution's data was split across multiple unitids | Recipient count at that unitid may undercount total institutional recipients | Consider filtering to `allocation_flag == 0` or documenting the limitation; check prevalence |
| `grant_type` | Portal encodes as integer, not string | Using string filters like `"Pell"` will silently return zero rows | Always use integer code: `grant_type == 1` |

---

## CAVEATS

### 1. FSA Does NOT Provide Enrollment Denominators

This is the single most important caveat for computing Pell share. The FSA grants dataset provides:
- **Pell recipient count** (`grant_recipients_unitid` where `grant_type == 1`)
- **Pell disbursement amount** (`value_grants_disbursed_unitid` where `grant_type == 1`)

It does NOT provide total enrollment. To compute "share of students receiving Pell Grants," you must join to an external enrollment source. See the PATTERNS section for denominator recommendations.

### 2. Pell Is Undergraduate-Only

Pell Grants are restricted to undergraduate students. The Pell recipient count therefore reflects undergraduate Pell recipients only. The denominator for Pell share should be **undergraduate enrollment** (not total enrollment including graduate students). Using total enrollment would systematically understate Pell share at institutions with large graduate programs.

### 3. Year-Round Pell (Post-2017)

Beginning in 2017-18, students can receive up to 150% of their scheduled Pell award in a single award year (enabling summer enrollment). This may cause:
- Slight inflation in recipient counts if a student receives multiple disbursements coded as separate records
- Higher total disbursement amounts per student
- Impact is likely small for Pell share computation (since it affects counts, not the population denominator) but should be documented

### 4. Award Year Definition

FSA `year` represents the academic award year starting July 1 (e.g., `year == 2020` means the 2020-21 award year, July 1 2020 through June 30 2021). This differs from:
- IPEDS fall enrollment (typically October snapshot)
- IPEDS graduation rates (cohort-based, with specific cohort start year)
- IPEDS admissions (for a specific entering class)

When joining FSA to IPEDS, the `year` field may not perfectly align. Typically, FSA `year == 2019` (AY 2019-20) aligns with IPEDS fall 2019 enrollment data, but verify this alignment for the specific analysis.

### 5. Data Lag

FSA data in the Portal extends through 2021. If the analysis requires years beyond 2021, this source is insufficient. For graduation rate and admissions data from IPEDS that may extend to more recent years, there will be a gap where FSA Pell data is unavailable for the latest IPEDS years.

### 6. Allocation Flag Institutions

Some institutions have `allocation_flag == 1`, meaning their data was allocated across multiple unitids (e.g., multi-campus systems). For these institutions, the Pell recipient count at any single unitid may be an allocated portion rather than a directly reported figure. This could introduce noise.

### 7. Coverage: Title IV Participants Only

FSA data only includes institutions participating in Title IV programs. Institutions not participating (rare among degree-granting institutions, but more common among short-term certificate programs) will have no FSA record. When joining to IPEDS, some IPEDS institutions may not appear in FSA data.

### 8. Suppression Patterns

Missing data code `-3` indicates suppression due to small cell sizes. For Pell grants specifically, suppression is relatively uncommon because Pell is the most widely used federal grant program and most institutions have sufficient recipients to avoid suppression. However, very small institutions or those with very few Pell recipients may have suppressed values.

**Typical suppression rates for Pell in the grants dataset:** LOW — Pell is the highest-volume grant program. Suppression is more common for smaller programs (TEACH Grant, Iraq/Afghanistan Service Grant, Children of Fallen Heroes). The `-1` (not reported) code is more likely than `-3` for Pell, indicating that the institution simply did not report rather than that values were suppressed.

### 9. Cross-State Comparability

FSA data is nationally comparable for Pell share analysis. Pell Grant eligibility and award calculations are federally standardized (based on SAI/EFC, cost of attendance, and enrollment intensity). There are no state-level variations in how Pell is administered. However, state-level financial aid policies (state grants, tuition levels) affect which students enroll and where, indirectly affecting institutional Pell share.

---

## PATTERNS

### Recommended Pattern: Computing Pell Share per Institution

**Step 1: Fetch and filter FSA grants to Pell only**

```python
# Filter grants to Pell Grant (grant_type == 1)
df_pell = df_grants.filter(
    (pl.col("grant_type") == 1) &
    (pl.col("grant_recipients_unitid") > 0)  # Exclude sentinel values -1, -2, -3 and zero
)
# Result: one row per (unitid, year) with Pell recipient count and disbursement
```

**Step 2: Join to IPEDS enrollment for denominator**

The recommended denominator for Pell share is **IPEDS undergraduate enrollment** (not total enrollment). This is because Pell is exclusively an undergraduate program.

```
Pell share = grant_recipients_unitid (where grant_type == 1) / IPEDS undergraduate enrollment
```

**Denominator options ranked:**

| Option | Source | Pros | Cons | Recommendation |
|--------|--------|------|------|----------------|
| IPEDS undergraduate enrollment (12-month) | IPEDS enrollment | Matches the award-year concept (full year); includes part-time students | May include non-degree-seeking students | **Best for FSA Pell share** |
| IPEDS undergraduate enrollment (fall) | IPEDS enrollment | Standard snapshot; widely used | Misses spring/summer-only students | **Acceptable alternative** |
| IPEDS total enrollment | IPEDS enrollment | Easy to compute | Includes graduate students, systematically deflating Pell share at research universities | **Not recommended** |
| FSA's own counts | FSA data | No join needed | FSA does not provide total enrollment — only recipient counts per aid type | **Not available** |

**Step 3: Join pattern**

```python
# Join FSA Pell to IPEDS enrollment on (unitid, year)
df_merged = df_pell.join(
    df_ipeds_enrollment.select(["unitid", "year", "undergrad_enrollment"]),
    on=["unitid", "year"],
    how="inner"
)

# Compute Pell share
df_merged = df_merged.with_columns(
    (pl.col("grant_recipients_unitid") / pl.col("undergrad_enrollment"))
    .alias("pell_share")
)
```

### Join Pattern: FSA to IPEDS

| Source 1 | Source 2 | Join Key | Expected Cardinality | Common Issues |
|----------|----------|----------|---------------------|---------------|
| FSA Grants (filtered to Pell) | IPEDS Directory/Enrollment | `unitid` + `year` | 1:1 after filtering to grant_type==1 | Some IPEDS institutions may lack FSA records (non-Title IV); some FSA institutions may have closed and lack IPEDS records; year alignment (FSA award year vs IPEDS fall year) |
| FSA Grants (filtered to Pell) | IPEDS Admissions | `unitid` + `year` | 1:1 | Admissions data is only for first-time degree-seeking undergrads; year alignment matters |
| FSA Grants (filtered to Pell) | IPEDS Graduation Rates | `unitid` + `year` | 1:1 (but cohort year logic differs) | Graduation rate `year` is cohort start year; FSA `year` is disbursement year — NOT the same concept |

### Join Key Compatibility

The FSA `unitid` is the same 6-digit IPEDS institution identifier used across all Education Data Portal datasets. It is directly joinable to:
- IPEDS Directory (`unitid`)
- IPEDS Enrollment (`unitid`)
- IPEDS Admissions (`unitid`)
- IPEDS Graduation Rates (`unitid`)
- College Scorecard (`unitid`)

**Known compatibility issue:** Some institutions have multiple OPEIDs but a single unitid (or vice versa). The `allocation_flag` and `combined_flag` in FSA data indicate when data has been split or combined across identifiers. For most analyses, using `unitid` and the `*_unitid` suffixed variables provides the correct institutional-level aggregation.

---

## PITFALLS

### Critical Pitfall 1: Using Total Enrollment Instead of Undergraduate Enrollment as Pell Share Denominator

**Risk:** Systematically underestimating Pell share at research universities and graduate-heavy institutions.

**Detection:** After computing Pell share, check if research universities (R1/R2) have suspiciously low Pell shares compared to known benchmarks. A typical 4-year institution has 30-40% Pell share; if R1 universities show 10-15%, the denominator likely includes graduate students.

**Avoidance:** Always use undergraduate-specific enrollment from IPEDS as the denominator. Verify by checking that Pell share values are reasonable (typically 15-80% for most institutions).

### Critical Pitfall 2: Failing to Filter Out Sentinel Values (-1, -2, -3)

**Risk:** Including sentinel values in aggregations (sums, means) will produce incorrect results. A `-1` in `grant_recipients_unitid` is NOT "negative one recipient" — it means "not reported."

**Detection:** Check for negative values in recipient count and disbursement columns before any aggregation. Run `df.filter(pl.col("grant_recipients_unitid") < 0).shape` to see how many rows have sentinel values.

**Avoidance:** Always filter to `> 0` or explicitly exclude `-1, -2, -3` before computing sums, means, or ratios.

### Critical Pitfall 3: Year Misalignment Between FSA and IPEDS Graduation Rates

**Risk:** IPEDS graduation rates are cohort-based (e.g., `year == 2014` means the cohort that started in fall 2014, with 6-year graduation measured in 2020). FSA `year == 2020` means the 2020-21 award year. If the analysis aims to associate Pell share with graduation rates, the analyst must decide which FSA year to use — the cohort start year or the graduation measurement year.

**Detection:** Look for implausible or weak correlations that may stem from temporal misalignment.

**Avoidance:** For a selectivity/graduation rate analysis, the most defensible approach is to use FSA Pell data from approximately the same period as the graduation rate cohort's enrollment (e.g., for a cohort starting in 2014, use FSA year 2014 or nearby years). Alternatively, average Pell share across multiple years to smooth annual fluctuations.

### Critical Pitfall 4: Summing Across Aggregate and Detail Loan Types (Loans Dataset)

**Risk:** Not relevant to Pell share computation, but important if using loan data alongside grants. Loan type codes 3, 6, 9, and 14 are aggregate totals of their component types. Summing code 1 + code 2 + code 3 would double-count because code 3 = code 1 + code 2.

**Detection:** Check if aggregate loan totals appear suspiciously high.

**Avoidance:** Use either individual types (1,2,4,5,7,8) or aggregate types (3,6,9), never both.

### Pitfall 5: Ignoring the Allocation Flag

**Risk:** For institutions with `allocation_flag == 1`, the Pell recipient count at that unitid may be an allocated portion of a multi-campus system's total. This could result in understated or noise-affected Pell counts at specific campuses.

**Detection:** Check the prevalence of `allocation_flag == 1` in the data. If rare (<5% of institutions), the impact is minor.

**Avoidance:** Document the limitation. Optionally filter to `allocation_flag == 0` for a cleaner analysis, or keep all institutions and note that some counts are allocated.

### Pitfall 6: Using String Codes for Portal Integer-Encoded Variables

**Risk:** Filtering with `grant_type == "Pell"` or `grant_type == "1"` (string) will silently return zero rows because the Portal encodes all categoricals as integers.

**Detection:** If a filter returns unexpectedly zero rows, check whether integer vs. string encoding is the issue.

**Avoidance:** Always use integer codes: `pl.col("grant_type") == 1`.

| `null` | No data available | Exclude from calculations; record or field not present |

| `value_grants_disbursed_unitid` | Nominal dollars, not inflation-adjusted | Dollar comparisons across years are misleading without adjustment | Apply CPI adjustments if comparing dollar amounts across years; for Pell share (count-based), this is not relevant |
| `allocation_flag` | When `1`, the institution's data was split across multiple unitids | Recipient count at that unitid may undercount total institutional recipients | Consider filtering to `allocation_flag == 0` or documenting the limitation; check prevalence |

## CAVEATS

### 1. FSA Does NOT Provide Enrollment Denominators

This is the single most important caveat for computing Pell share. The FSA grants dataset provides:
- **Pell recipient count** (`grant_recipients_unitid` where `grant_type == 1`)
- **Pell disbursement amount** (`value_grants_disbursed_unitid` where `grant_type == 1`)

It does NOT provide total enrollment. To compute "share of students receiving Pell Grants," you must join to an external enrollment source. See the PATTERNS section for denominator recommendations.

### 2. Pell Is Undergraduate-Only

Pell Grants are restricted to undergraduate students. The Pell recipient count therefore reflects undergraduate Pell recipients only. The denominator for Pell share should be **undergraduate enrollment** (not total enrollment including graduate students). Using total enrollment would systematically understate Pell share at institutions with large graduate programs.

### 3. Year-Round Pell (Post-2017)

Beginning in 2017-18, students can receive up to 150% of their scheduled Pell award in a single award year (enabling summer enrollment). This may cause:
- Slight inflation in recipient counts if a student receives multiple disbursements coded as separate records
- Higher total disbursement amounts per student
- Impact is likely small for Pell share computation (since it affects counts, not the population denominator) but should be documented

### 4. Award Year Definition

FSA `year` represents the academic award year starting July 1 (e.g., `year == 2020` means the 2020-21 award year, July 1 2020 through June 30 2021). This differs from:
- IPEDS fall enrollment (typically October snapshot)
- IPEDS graduation rates (cohort-based, with specific cohort start year)
- IPEDS admissions (for a specific entering class)

When joining FSA to IPEDS, the `year` field may not perfectly align. Typically, FSA `year == 2019` (AY 2019-20) aligns with IPEDS fall 2019 enrollment data, but verify this alignment for the specific analysis.

### 5. Data Lag

FSA data in the Portal extends through 2021. If the analysis requires years beyond 2021, this source is insufficient. For graduation rate and admissions data from IPEDS that may extend to more recent years, there will be a gap where FSA Pell data is unavailable for the latest IPEDS years.

### 6. Allocation Flag Institutions

Some institutions have `allocation_flag == 1`, meaning their data was allocated across multiple unitids (e.g., multi-campus systems). For these institutions, the Pell recipient count at any single unitid may be an allocated portion rather than a directly reported figure. This could introduce noise.

### 7. Coverage: Title IV Participants Only

FSA data only includes institutions participating in Title IV programs. Institutions not participating (rare among degree-granting institutions, but more common among short-term certificate programs) will have no FSA record. When joining to IPEDS, some IPEDS institutions may not appear in FSA data.

### 8. Suppression Patterns

Missing data code `-3` indicates suppression due to small cell sizes. For Pell grants specifically, suppression is relatively uncommon because Pell is the most widely used federal grant program and most institutions have sufficient recipients to avoid suppression. However, very small institutions or those with very few Pell recipients may have suppressed values.

**Typical suppression rates for Pell in the grants dataset:** LOW — Pell is the highest-volume grant program. Suppression is more common for smaller programs (TEACH Grant, Iraq/Afghanistan Service Grant, Children of Fallen Heroes). The `-1` (not reported) code is more likely than `-3` for Pell, indicating that the institution simply did not report rather than that values were suppressed.

### 9. Cross-State Comparability

FSA data is nationally comparable for Pell share analysis. Pell Grant eligibility and award calculations are federally standardized (based on SAI/EFC, cost of attendance, and enrollment intensity). There are no state-level variations in how Pell is administered. However, state-level financial aid policies (state grants, tuition levels) affect which students enroll and where, indirectly affecting institutional Pell share.

## PATTERNS

### Recommended Pattern: Computing Pell Share per Institution

**Step 1: Fetch and filter FSA grants to Pell only**

```python
# Filter grants to Pell Grant (grant_type == 1)
df_pell = df_grants.filter(
    (pl.col("grant_type") == 1) &
    (pl.col("grant_recipients_unitid") > 0)  # Exclude sentinel values -1, -2, -3 and zero
)
# Result: one row per (unitid, year) with Pell recipient count and disbursement
```

**Step 2: Join to IPEDS enrollment for denominator**

The recommended denominator for Pell share is **IPEDS undergraduate enrollment** (not total enrollment). This is because Pell is exclusively an undergraduate program.

```
Pell share = grant_recipients_unitid (where grant_type == 1) / IPEDS undergraduate enrollment
```

**Denominator options ranked:**

| Option | Source | Pros | Cons | Recommendation |
|--------|--------|------|------|----------------|
| IPEDS undergraduate enrollment (12-month) | IPEDS enrollment | Matches the award-year concept (full year); includes part-time students | May include non-degree-seeking students | **Best for FSA Pell share** |
| IPEDS undergraduate enrollment (fall) | IPEDS enrollment | Standard snapshot; widely used | Misses spring/summer-only students | **Acceptable alternative** |
| IPEDS total enrollment | IPEDS enrollment | Easy to compute | Includes graduate students, systematically deflating Pell share at research universities | **Not recommended** |
| FSA's own counts | FSA data | No join needed | FSA does not provide total enrollment — only recipient counts per aid type | **Not available** |

**Step 3: Join pattern**

```python
# Join FSA Pell to IPEDS enrollment on (unitid, year)
df_merged = df_pell.join(
    df_ipeds_enrollment.select(["unitid", "year", "undergrad_enrollment"]),
    on=["unitid", "year"],
    how="inner"
)

# Compute Pell share
df_merged = df_merged.with_columns(
    (pl.col("grant_recipients_unitid") / pl.col("undergrad_enrollment"))
    .alias("pell_share")
)
```

### Join Pattern: FSA to IPEDS

| Source 1 | Source 2 | Join Key | Expected Cardinality | Common Issues |
|----------|----------|----------|---------------------|---------------|
| FSA Grants (filtered to Pell) | IPEDS Directory/Enrollment | `unitid` + `year` | 1:1 after filtering to grant_type==1 | Some IPEDS institutions may lack FSA records (non-Title IV); some FSA institutions may have closed and lack IPEDS records; year alignment (FSA award year vs IPEDS fall year) |
| FSA Grants (filtered to Pell) | IPEDS Admissions | `unitid` + `year` | 1:1 | Admissions data is only for first-time degree-seeking undergrads; year alignment matters |
| FSA Grants (filtered to Pell) | IPEDS Graduation Rates | `unitid` + `year` | 1:1 (but cohort year logic differs) | Graduation rate `year` is cohort start year; FSA `year` is disbursement year — NOT the same concept |

### Join Key Compatibility

The FSA `unitid` is the same 6-digit IPEDS institution identifier used across all Education Data Portal datasets. It is directly joinable to:
- IPEDS Directory (`unitid`)
- IPEDS Enrollment (`unitid`)
- IPEDS Admissions (`unitid`)
- IPEDS Graduation Rates (`unitid`)
- College Scorecard (`unitid`)

**Known compatibility issue:** Some institutions have multiple OPEIDs but a single unitid (or vice versa). The `allocation_flag` and `combined_flag` in FSA data indicate when data has been split or combined across identifiers. For most analyses, using `unitid` and the `*_unitid` suffixed variables provides the correct institutional-level aggregation.

## PITFALLS

### Critical Pitfall 1: Using Total Enrollment Instead of Undergraduate Enrollment as Pell Share Denominator

**Risk:** Systematically underestimating Pell share at research universities and graduate-heavy institutions.

**Detection:** After computing Pell share, check if research universities (R1/R2) have suspiciously low Pell shares compared to known benchmarks. A typical 4-year institution has 30-40% Pell share; if R1 universities show 10-15%, the denominator likely includes graduate students.

**Avoidance:** Always use undergraduate-specific enrollment from IPEDS as the denominator. Verify by checking that Pell share values are reasonable (typically 15-80% for most institutions).

### Critical Pitfall 2: Failing to Filter Out Sentinel Values (-1, -2, -3)

**Risk:** Including sentinel values in aggregations (sums, means) will produce incorrect results. A `-1` in `grant_recipients_unitid` is NOT "negative one recipient" — it means "not reported."

**Detection:** Check for negative values in recipient count and disbursement columns before any aggregation. Run `df.filter(pl.col("grant_recipients_unitid") < 0).shape` to see how many rows have sentinel values.

**Avoidance:** Always filter to `> 0` or explicitly exclude `-1, -2, -3` before computing sums, means, or ratios.

### Critical Pitfall 3: Year Misalignment Between FSA and IPEDS Graduation Rates

**Risk:** IPEDS graduation rates are cohort-based (e.g., `year == 2014` means the cohort that started in fall 2014, with 6-year graduation measured in 2020). FSA `year == 2020` means the 2020-21 award year. If the analysis aims to associate Pell share with graduation rates, the analyst must decide which FSA year to use — the cohort start year or the graduation measurement year.

**Detection:** Look for implausible or weak correlations that may stem from temporal misalignment.

**Avoidance:** For a selectivity/graduation rate analysis, the most defensible approach is to use FSA Pell data from approximately the same period as the graduation rate cohort's enrollment (e.g., for a cohort starting in 2014, use FSA year 2014 or nearby years). Alternatively, average Pell share across multiple years to smooth annual fluctuations.

### Critical Pitfall 4: Summing Across Aggregate and Detail Loan Types (Loans Dataset)

**Risk:** Not relevant to Pell share computation, but important if using loan data alongside grants. Loan type codes 3, 6, 9, and 14 are aggregate totals of their component types. Summing code 1 + code 2 + code 3 would double-count because code 3 = code 1 + code 2.

**Detection:** Check if aggregate loan totals appear suspiciously high.

**Avoidance:** Use either individual types (1,2,4,5,7,8) or aggregate types (3,6,9), never both.

### Pitfall 5: Ignoring the Allocation Flag

**Risk:** For institutions with `allocation_flag == 1`, the Pell recipient count at that unitid may be an allocated portion of a multi-campus system's total. This could result in understated or noise-affected Pell counts at specific campuses.

**Detection:** Check the prevalence of `allocation_flag == 1` in the data. If rare (<5% of institutions), the impact is minor.

**Avoidance:** Document the limitation. Optionally filter to `allocation_flag == 0` for a cleaner analysis, or keep all institutions and note that some counts are allocated.

### Pitfall 6: Using String Codes for Portal Integer-Encoded Variables

**Risk:** Filtering with `grant_type == "Pell"` or `grant_type == "1"` (string) will silently return zero rows because the Portal encodes all categoricals as integers.

**Detection:** If a filter returns unexpectedly zero rows, check whether integer vs. string encoding is the issue.

**Avoidance:** Always use integer codes: `pl.col("grant_type") == 1`.

**Impact:** The student characteristics data (pct_first_gen, family income, dependency status) from Scorecard are too old for a 2020-2021 analysis. The student body composition at many institutions changed significantly between 2016 and 2020-2021, particularly due to enrollment shifts and COVID-19 impacts.

**Mitigation:** Use IPEDS for student demographics (enrollment by race, Pell shares from SFA survey) which have 2020-2021 data. Only use Scorecard for variables IPEDS cannot provide (earnings, repayment, detailed family income distributions).

### 2. Title IV Population Bias (CRITICAL)

Scorecard tracks ONLY students who received federal financial aid. Coverage varies dramatically:

| Institution Type | Typical Title IV Coverage | Bias Direction |
|-----------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| For-profit colleges | 80-95% | Near-complete; data representative |
| Community colleges | 60-80% | Moderate gap |
| Public 4-year (non-flagship) | 60-75% | Moderate gap |
| Public flagships | 50-70% | Significant gap |
| Private non-profit | 50-70% | Significant gap |
| Elite/selective privates | 30-50% | **Large gap -- data covers minority of students** |

**Impact on this analysis:** Since we are analyzing the relationship between graduation rates and *selectivity*, the most selective institutions have the lowest Scorecard coverage. At an elite private with 35% Title IV coverage, Scorecard demographics represent a systematically different subpopulation (lower-income, more likely first-gen, more likely URM) than the full student body. This creates a correlation between selectivity and measurement bias that directly confounds our analysis.

**Direction of bias by metric:**
- Earnings: **understated** (excludes higher-income full-pay students)
- Debt: **overstated** (by definition; non-borrowers excluded)
- Completion: **understated** (lower-income students face more completion barriers)
- Demographics: **biased toward lower-income** students

**Mitigation:** Use IPEDS for demographic variables that cover the full student body. If using Scorecard earnings as an alternative outcome, note that selectivity-earnings comparisons have built-in bias (more selective = lower coverage = more biased sample).

### 3. Completion Rates Not in Portal

The Portal does NOT have a separate Scorecard completion rates dataset. Completion variables (`C150_4`, etc.) are only in the original Scorecard bulk downloads at `collegescorecard.ed.gov`.

**Impact:** For graduation rate analysis, we must use IPEDS graduation rates (`ipeds/colleges_ipeds_grad-rates`), not Scorecard.

**Mitigation:** This is not a problem -- IPEDS is the standard source for graduation rates. But it means Scorecard adds less value to this particular analysis than initially expected.

### 4. Earnings Data Excludes Key Populations

Earnings are measured only for students who are:
- Working (have W-2 income)
- NOT enrolled in further education

This means:
- Graduate school students are excluded (fields with high grad school rates like biology, pre-law show *inflated* earnings because low earners are still in school)
- Self-employed individuals (1099 income) are excluded
- Non-working individuals are excluded

### 5. Data Lag in Earnings

6-year earnings reflect students who entered 7+ years before the data release. 10-year earnings reflect students from 11+ years ago. For the Portal data (earnings through 2018), the 6-year earnings in the most recent year would reflect an entry cohort from approximately 2012 -- nearly a decade before our target analysis period.

### 6. Pandemic Effects (2020-2023)

Default and repayment data from 2020-2023 are distorted by the federal payment pause:
- $0 payments counted as "on track"
- CDR (cohort default rate) artificially low
- Forbearance protected from default

If using 2020 default data, it will not reflect normal repayment behavior.

### 7. Suppression Patterns

| Data Type | Typical Suppression Rate |
|-----------|--------------------------|
| Institution-level earnings | 5-15% |
| Disaggregated earnings (by income) | 30-50% |
| Field-of-study earnings | 40-60% |
| Small institution data | 20-40% |

Suppression threshold: fewer than 30 students with positive earnings leads to suppression. This disproportionately affects small and specialized institutions.

---

## PATTERNS

### Recommended Fetch Pattern for Earnings

```python
# Portal uses LONG format -- filter by years_after_entry, not wide column names
earnings = fetch_from_mirrors("scorecard/colleges_scorecard_earnings")
six_yr = earnings.filter(pl.col("years_after_entry") == 6)
valid = six_yr.filter(
    pl.col("earnings_med").is_not_null() &
    (pl.col("earnings_med") != -3) &
    (pl.col("earnings_med") > 0)
)
```

### Join Pattern: Scorecard Earnings to IPEDS

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Join key | `unitid` (IPEDS institution ID, present in all Scorecard datasets) |
| Cardinality | Many-to-one from Scorecard earnings (multiple years/time horizons) to IPEDS directory (one row per institution per year) |
| Common issue | Scorecard earnings dataset does NOT contain institution name, control type, or state -- must join to `scorecard/colleges_scorecard_inst_characteristics` or IPEDS directory |
| Year alignment | Scorecard `year` column may not align with IPEDS `year` due to different lag structures; use closest available year |

### Join Pattern: Scorecard Student Body to Earnings

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| Join key | `unitid` + `year` |
| Cardinality | One-to-many (student body is one row per institution-year; earnings has multiple rows per institution-year for different time horizons) |
| Common issue | Year ranges differ: student body ends 2016, earnings has 2018 data |

### Pattern: Validating Title IV Coverage

Compare Scorecard FAFSA applicant counts to IPEDS total enrollment to estimate what fraction of students are represented:

```python
coverage = scorecard_nslds["count_total_FAFSA_applicants"] / ipeds_enrollment["total_enrollment"]
# Flag institutions with < 50% coverage for special handling
```

---

## PITFALLS

### Pitfall 1: Using Scorecard for Variables That IPEDS Provides Better (CRITICAL)

**The mistake:** Fetching `student_body_nslds` for Pell share, racial demographics, or enrollment composition.

**Why it breaks:** (a) Pell share (`PCTPELL`) is NOT in the Portal Scorecard datasets. (b) Racial enrollment shares (`UGDS_BLACK`, `UGDS_HISP`) are NOT in the Portal Scorecard datasets. (c) Even the variables that ARE available (like `first_gen_student_pct`) only go through 2016 and cover only Title IV recipients. IPEDS provides these for the full student body with more recent years.

**Detection:** Check column listings before building fetch scripts. The Portal Scorecard has only 6 datasets with specific column sets documented in the skill.

**Avoidance:** Use IPEDS for: enrollment by race (`fall-enrollment`), Pell share (`sfa`), admission rates (`admissions`), control type (`directory`), graduation rates (`grad-rates`). Use Scorecard ONLY for: earnings, debt, repayment, default, family income details, first-gen share (if 2016 data is acceptable).

### Pitfall 2: Treating `-3` as a Valid Numeric Value in Earnings

**The mistake:** Computing `mean(earnings_med)` without filtering out `-3` suppression codes.

**Why it breaks:** `-3` is an integer code, not a valid earnings value. Including it drastically reduces computed averages. For example, ~24,000 rows in the earnings dataset have `-3` in `earnings_mean`.

**Detection:** Check for negative values in earnings columns: `df.filter(pl.col("earnings_med") < 0)`. If you see `-3` values, suppression codes are present.

**Avoidance:** Always apply the triple filter: `is_not_null() & != -3 & > 0`.

### Pitfall 3: Using Wide-Format Variable Names on Portal Data

**The mistake:** Looking for columns named `MD_EARN_WNE_P6` or `PCTPELL` in Portal data.

**Why it breaks:** The Portal restructured Scorecard data into LONG format with lowercase names. `MD_EARN_WNE_P6` becomes `earnings_med` filtered by `years_after_entry == 6`. The column literally does not exist.

**Detection:** Column not found errors. The Portal column names are all lowercase.

**Avoidance:** Consult the variable-definitions reference. Always use Portal column names (lowercase, LONG format).

### Pitfall 4: Conflating Home ZIP Demographics with Student Demographics (Treasury Dataset)

**The mistake:** Using `black_home_zip_pct` from the Treasury dataset as a proxy for Black student enrollment share.

**Why it breaks:** These are ecological measures of the neighborhoods students come from, not student-level demographics. A student from a predominantly Black ZIP code is not necessarily Black, and the composition of home ZIPs tells you about where aid recipients grew up, not the student body composition.

**Detection:** Variable names containing `_home_zip_` are neighborhood-level measures.

**Avoidance:** Use IPEDS enrollment data for student-level racial demographics.

### Pitfall 5: Assuming Earnings Data Represents All Students

**The mistake:** Claiming "graduates of Institution X earn $Y" without qualifying that this covers only Title IV recipients who are working and not enrolled.

**Why it breaks:** At selective private institutions, Scorecard covers only 30-50% of students. The excluded students (full-pay, international) likely have different outcomes. Earnings also exclude self-employed, graduate school attendees, and non-workers.

**Detection:** Check institution-level Title IV coverage by comparing FAFSA applicant counts to IPEDS enrollment.

**Avoidance:** Always qualify: "Among Title IV aid recipients who were working and not enrolled in further education..."

### Pitfall 6: Comparing Scorecard Completion Rates to IPEDS Graduation Rates

**The mistake:** Treating Scorecard completion metrics and IPEDS graduation rates as interchangeable.

**Why it breaks:** Different populations (Title IV recipients vs. first-time full-time), different tracking methods (NSLDS system-wide vs. single institution), different inclusion of part-time and transfer students.

**Detection:** If you are joining Scorecard completion to IPEDS graduation rates, you are comparing apples to oranges.

**Avoidance:** Pick one source for graduation/completion rates and use it consistently. For this analysis, IPEDS graduation rates are the standard and more appropriate choice.

---

**Overall Confidence:** MEDIUM

**LOW Confidence Items Requiring Resolution:** None at LOW confidence. However, the MEDIUM confidence on PATTERNS should be addressed during data fetch/join steps by verifying match rates empirically.

## Learning Signal

**Learning Signal:** Data -- College Scorecard Portal datasets lack key demographic variables (Pell share, racial enrollment) that exist in original Scorecard bulk downloads but are served through IPEDS in the Portal architecture; student characteristics data ends 2016, making it unsuitable for 2020-2021 analysis.

---

## Recommendations for Analysis

Based on this source research, specific to the question "What is the relationship between college graduation rates and institutional selectivity?":

### 1. DO NOT use Scorecard for primary demographic variables

Use IPEDS for Pell share, racial enrollment, admission rates, and graduation rates. IPEDS has 2020-2021 data, covers the full student body, and is the standard source for these metrics. Scorecard adds nothing for these variables in the Portal.

### 2. Consider Scorecard earnings as an OPTIONAL enrichment, not a core variable

Scorecard earnings could serve as an interesting alternative "institutional quality" outcome alongside graduation rates. However:
- The Title IV coverage bias means earnings are measured for a non-representative subsample, especially at selective institutions
- The data lag means earnings reflect old cohorts
- Portal earnings data has a gap (2015-2017) and the 2018 data point needs verification
- This adds complexity without being essential to the core research question

**Recommendation:** Do NOT include Scorecard earnings in the initial analysis. If the researcher wants to explore earnings as a secondary outcome after the core graduation-rate analysis is complete, it can be added as a sensitivity check with appropriate caveats.

### 3. If Scorecard is used at all, only for unique variables IPEDS cannot provide

The only unique value Scorecard adds (that IPEDS cannot) is:
- Actual IRS-linked earnings data (unique to Scorecard)
- Detailed family income distributions (tercile breakdowns)
- First-generation student share (though only through 2016)

For this analysis focused on graduation rates and selectivity, none of these are essential.

### 4. Prioritize IPEDS as the single postsecondary source

Using IPEDS for all variables (directory, admissions, graduation rates, enrollment by race, student financial aid for Pell share, institutional finance for resources) provides:
- Consistent year coverage (2020-2021 available)
- Full student body coverage (not just Title IV recipients)
- Standard join key (`unitid`) across all IPEDS surveys
- No population coverage bias confound

### 5. If earnings are desired as secondary outcome, document limitations prominently

Any earnings analysis must note:
- Title IV recipients only (30-50% at selective privates)
- Working and not enrolled only (excludes grad school, self-employed, non-workers)
- 6-year earnings reflect cohorts from ~2012 entry
- Systematic coverage bias correlates with selectivity (the key independent variable)

- **Proceed?** YES -- but with the strong recommendation to use IPEDS rather than Scorecard for the core analysis variables. Scorecard should be treated as optional enrichment only, not a required data source.

### 3. Population Coverage Bias Assessment

The Title IV limitation is the single most consequential caveat for this analysis. The bias is not random -- it is *systematically correlated with selectivity*:

**At highly selective institutions (admission rate <20%):** Title IV coverage is typically 30-50%. The excluded 50-70% are disproportionately: full-pay students from high-income families, international students, students with only institutional/private aid. These excluded students likely have higher family resources, different demographic profiles, and potentially different graduation trajectories.

**At moderately selective institutions (admission rate 40-60%):** Coverage is 60-75%. The bias exists but is smaller.

**At open-access institutions (admission rate >80%):** Coverage is 70-90%+. Scorecard data is reasonably representative.

**Net effect on this analysis:** If we used Scorecard demographics to measure "student body composition" across the selectivity spectrum, we would be measuring *different fractions of the student body* at each selectivity level. At selective schools, we would see a sample skewed toward lower-income students; at open-access schools, we would see nearly the full student body. This creates a systematic confound between selectivity and the population being measured -- exactly the confound this analysis needs to avoid.

**Recommendation:** Use IPEDS, which reports for the full student body regardless of aid status.

### 4. Earnings Data Assessment

**Can earnings serve as an alternative outcome?** In principle, yes -- post-graduation earnings complement graduation rates as a measure of institutional "quality" or "value added." However, for this specific analysis, the practical obstacles are significant:

**Coverage:** The same Title IV coverage bias that affects student demographics also affects earnings. At selective privates with 35% coverage, reported median earnings reflect a non-representative minority of graduates.

**Year coverage:** Portal earnings cover 2003-2014 and 2018. There is no 2020-2021 earnings data. The 2018 data point reflects 6-year earnings for entry cohorts from approximately 2012 -- nearly a decade before our target.

**Population filter:** Earnings are computed only for those who are (a) working with W-2 income and (b) not enrolled in further education. For selective institutions that send many graduates to graduate school, this filter selectively removes a large fraction of graduates, further biasing the sample.

**Unique value:** Despite these limitations, Scorecard is the ONLY source of IRS-linked actual earnings data. No other federal source provides comparable institution-level earnings. If earnings analysis is desired, there is no substitute.

**Bottom line:** Earnings data could be a compelling secondary analysis but should not be part of the core graduation-rate/selectivity analysis due to coverage bias, staleness, and the compounding population filters. If pursued later, it requires extensive documentation of limitations.

### 5. Critical Warnings

1. **`pct_pell`, `pct_black`, `pct_hispanic`, and `ADM_RATE` are NOT available in Portal Scorecard datasets.** These must come from IPEDS. The Stage 2 finding that Scorecard `student_body_nslds` provides these was incorrect for the Portal architecture.

2. **The Scorecard earnings dataset uses `-3` integer codes for suppression, NOT null.** Any statistical computation that does not explicitly filter `-3` will produce corrupt results. Approximately 24,000 rows have this code.

3. **Home ZIP demographics (Treasury dataset) are ecological measures, not student demographics.** Do not use `black_home_zip_pct` as a proxy for Black student enrollment.

4. **The year gap problem is real and severe for student characteristics.** The Portal student body datasets end at 2016. For a 2020-2021 analysis, this is a 4-5 year gap during a period of significant change in higher education.

### 6. Recommendation: Use Scorecard or IPEDS Alternatives?

**Clear recommendation: Use IPEDS as the primary and likely sole postsecondary data source for this analysis.**

| Variable Need | Source | Rationale |
|--------------|--------|-----------|
| Graduation rates | IPEDS `grad-rates` | Standard source; 2020-2021 available; full FTFT cohort |
| Admission rates (selectivity) | IPEDS `admissions` | Standard source; only place to get it |
| Pell share | IPEDS `sfa` | Full student body; 2020-2021 available |
| URM enrollment | IPEDS `fall-enrollment` | Full student body; 2020-2021 available |
| Institutional resources (student-faculty ratio, expenditures) | IPEDS `directory`, `finance` | Standard source |
| Institutional control, sector | IPEDS `directory` | Standard source |
| Earnings (OPTIONAL secondary outcome) | Scorecard `earnings` | Only source; add only if researcher wants it; document limitations extensively |

**Scorecard adds unique value only for earnings.** Everything else this analysis needs is better sourced from IPEDS.

### 7. Confidence Assessment

| Finding | Confidence | Rationale |
|---------|------------|-----------|
| Key demographic variables NOT in Portal Scorecard | HIGH | Explicitly documented in skill; column listings verified empirically during ingestion |
| Student characteristics end at 2016 | HIGH | Year ranges confirmed in skill metadata from actual data profiling |
| Title IV coverage rates by institution type | MEDIUM | Ranges are approximate (from skill reference), not computed from actual data; widely cited in literature |
| Earnings as alternative outcome assessment | MEDIUM | Based on documented limitations; actual suppression rates and coverage for our specific institution set not yet computed |
| Recommendation to use IPEDS over Scorecard | HIGH | Based on comprehensive variable availability analysis showing IPEDS covers all core needs with recent data and full population |

**Overall Confidence:** MEDIUM-HIGH (individual findings are well-supported; the MEDIUM rating reflects that some details like exact suppression rates for our target population need empirical verification)

**LOW Confidence Items Requiring Resolution:** None at LOW confidence. The key finding -- that Scorecard should not be a primary source for this analysis -- is supported at HIGH confidence from multiple converging evidence points.

## CAVEATS

### 1. Year Coverage Gap (CRITICAL for This Analysis)

| Dataset | Portal Years | Target Year | Gap |
|---------|-------------|-------------|-----|
| Student Body NSLDS | 1997-2016 | 2020-2021 | **4-5 years stale** |
| Student Body Treasury | 1997-2016 | 2020-2021 | **4-5 years stale** |
| Earnings | 2003-2014, 2018 | 2020-2021 | **Non-continuous; 2018 is closest** |
| Default (FSA) | 1996-2020 | 2020-2021 | Close match |
| Inst Characteristics | 1996-2020 | 2020-2021 | Close match |
| Repayment (NSLDS) | 2007-2016 | 2020-2021 | **4-5 years stale** |

**Impact:** The student characteristics data (pct_first_gen, family income, dependency status) from Scorecard are too old for a 2020-2021 analysis. The student body composition at many institutions changed significantly between 2016 and 2020-2021, particularly due to enrollment shifts and COVID-19 impacts.

**Mitigation:** Use IPEDS for student demographics (enrollment by race, Pell shares from SFA survey) which have 2020-2021 data. Only use Scorecard for variables IPEDS cannot provide (earnings, repayment, detailed family income distributions).

### 2. Title IV Population Bias (CRITICAL)

Scorecard tracks ONLY students who received federal financial aid. Coverage varies dramatically:

| Institution Type | Typical Title IV Coverage | Bias Direction |
|-----------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| For-profit colleges | 80-95% | Near-complete; data representative |
| Community colleges | 60-80% | Moderate gap |
| Public 4-year (non-flagship) | 60-75% | Moderate gap |
| Public flagships | 50-70% | Significant gap |
| Private non-profit | 50-70% | Significant gap |
| Elite/selective privates | 30-50% | **Large gap -- data covers minority of students** |

**Impact on this analysis:** Since we are analyzing the relationship between graduation rates and *selectivity*, the most selective institutions have the lowest Scorecard coverage. At an elite private with 35% Title IV coverage, Scorecard demographics represent a systematically different subpopulation (lower-income, more likely first-gen, more likely URM) than the full student body. This creates a correlation between selectivity and measurement bias that directly confounds our analysis.

**Direction of bias by metric:**
- Earnings: **understated** (excludes higher-income full-pay students)
- Debt: **overstated** (by definition; non-borrowers excluded)
- Completion: **understated** (lower-income students face more completion barriers)
- Demographics: **biased toward lower-income** students

**Mitigation:** Use IPEDS for demographic variables that cover the full student body. If using Scorecard earnings as an alternative outcome, note that selectivity-earnings comparisons have built-in bias (more selective = lower coverage = more biased sample).

### 3. Completion Rates Not in Portal

The Portal does NOT have a separate Scorecard completion rates dataset. Completion variables (`C150_4`, etc.) are only in the original Scorecard bulk downloads at `collegescorecard.ed.gov`.

**Impact:** For graduation rate analysis, we must use IPEDS graduation rates (`ipeds/colleges_ipeds_grad-rates`), not Scorecard.

**Mitigation:** This is not a problem -- IPEDS is the standard source for graduation rates. But it means Scorecard adds less value to this particular analysis than initially expected.

### 4. Earnings Data Excludes Key Populations

Earnings are measured only for students who are:
- Working (have W-2 income)
- NOT enrolled in further education

This means:
- Graduate school students are excluded (fields with high grad school rates like biology, pre-law show *inflated* earnings because low earners are still in school)
- Self-employed individuals (1099 income) are excluded
- Non-working individuals are excluded

### 5. Data Lag in Earnings

6-year earnings reflect students who entered 7+ years before the data release. 10-year earnings reflect students from 11+ years ago. For the Portal data (earnings through 2018), the 6-year earnings in the most recent year would reflect an entry cohort from approximately 2012 -- nearly a decade before our target analysis period.

### 6. Pandemic Effects (2020-2023)

Default and repayment data from 2020-2023 are distorted by the federal payment pause:
- $0 payments counted as "on track"
- CDR (cohort default rate) artificially low
- Forbearance protected from default

If using 2020 default data, it will not reflect normal repayment behavior.

### 7. Suppression Patterns

| Data Type | Typical Suppression Rate |
|-----------|--------------------------|
| Institution-level earnings | 5-15% |
| Disaggregated earnings (by income) | 30-50% |
| Field-of-study earnings | 40-60% |
| Small institution data | 20-40% |

Suppression threshold: fewer than 30 students with positive earnings leads to suppression. This disproportionately affects small and specialized institutions.

## PITFALLS

### Pitfall 1: Using Scorecard for Variables That IPEDS Provides Better (CRITICAL)

**The mistake:** Fetching `student_body_nslds` for Pell share, racial demographics, or enrollment composition.

**Why it breaks:** (a) Pell share (`PCTPELL`) is NOT in the Portal Scorecard datasets. (b) Racial enrollment shares (`UGDS_BLACK`, `UGDS_HISP`) are NOT in the Portal Scorecard datasets. (c) Even the variables that ARE available (like `first_gen_student_pct`) only go through 2016 and cover only Title IV recipients. IPEDS provides these for the full student body with more recent years.

**Detection:** Check column listings before building fetch scripts. The Portal Scorecard has only 6 datasets with specific column sets documented in the skill.

**Avoidance:** Use IPEDS for: enrollment by race (`fall-enrollment`), Pell share (`sfa`), admission rates (`admissions`), control type (`directory`), graduation rates (`grad-rates`). Use Scorecard ONLY for: earnings, debt, repayment, default, family income details, first-gen share (if 2016 data is acceptable).

### Pitfall 2: Treating `-3` as a Valid Numeric Value in Earnings

**The mistake:** Computing `mean(earnings_med)` without filtering out `-3` suppression codes.

**Why it breaks:** `-3` is an integer code, not a valid earnings value. Including it drastically reduces computed averages. For example, ~24,000 rows in the earnings dataset have `-3` in `earnings_mean`.

**Detection:** Check for negative values in earnings columns: `df.filter(pl.col("earnings_med") < 0)`. If you see `-3` values, suppression codes are present.

**Avoidance:** Always apply the triple filter: `is_not_null() & != -3 & > 0`.

### Pitfall 3: Using Wide-Format Variable Names on Portal Data

**The mistake:** Looking for columns named `MD_EARN_WNE_P6` or `PCTPELL` in Portal data.

**Why it breaks:** The Portal restructured Scorecard data into LONG format with lowercase names. `MD_EARN_WNE_P6` becomes `earnings_med` filtered by `years_after_entry == 6`. The column literally does not exist.

**Detection:** Column not found errors. The Portal column names are all lowercase.

**Avoidance:** Consult the variable-definitions reference. Always use Portal column names (lowercase, LONG format).

### Pitfall 4: Conflating Home ZIP Demographics with Student Demographics (Treasury Dataset)

**The mistake:** Using `black_home_zip_pct` from the Treasury dataset as a proxy for Black student enrollment share.

**Why it breaks:** These are ecological measures of the neighborhoods students come from, not student-level demographics. A student from a predominantly Black ZIP code is not necessarily Black, and the composition of home ZIPs tells you about where aid recipients grew up, not the student body composition.

**Detection:** Variable names containing `_home_zip_` are neighborhood-level measures.

**Avoidance:** Use IPEDS enrollment data for student-level racial demographics.

### Pitfall 5: Assuming Earnings Data Represents All Students

**The mistake:** Claiming "graduates of Institution X earn $Y" without qualifying that this covers only Title IV recipients who are working and not enrolled.

**Why it breaks:** At selective private institutions, Scorecard covers only 30-50% of students. The excluded students (full-pay, international) likely have different outcomes. Earnings also exclude self-employed, graduate school attendees, and non-workers.

**Detection:** Check institution-level Title IV coverage by comparing FAFSA applicant counts to IPEDS enrollment.

**Avoidance:** Always qualify: "Among Title IV aid recipients who were working and not enrolled in further education..."

### Pitfall 6: Comparing Scorecard Completion Rates to IPEDS Graduation Rates

**The mistake:** Treating Scorecard completion metrics and IPEDS graduation rates as interchangeable.

**Why it breaks:** Different populations (Title IV recipients vs. first-time full-time), different tracking methods (NSLDS system-wide vs. single institution), different inclusion of part-time and transfer students.

**Detection:** If you are joining Scorecard completion to IPEDS graduation rates, you are comparing apples to oranges.

**Avoidance:** Pick one source for graduation/completion rates and use it consistently. For this analysis, IPEDS graduation rates are the standard and more appropriate choice.
